newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt to stall vote on Cardosa second term.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt to stall vote on Cardosa second term.

text.p: A panel in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies is officially scheduled to vote on Tuesday on a proposal allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for a second term.

But an official said the vote will in fact be delayed until January as part of the government's strategy for approval of the constitutional amendment which would permit re-election for sitting presidents, state governors and mayors.
"There's no way they're going to vote today," said the official, an aide to the government's leader in the lower house, Dep. Benito Gama.

The aide said deputies allied to the government would instead ask for more time to study the amendment, denying opposition members the chance to do likewise in early January when the government wants the panel to vote on re-election.

Government leaders expect the amendment to be approved by the panel around January 8 without difficulties. They are currently mustering support for the next, bigger hurdle -- two three-fifth majorities on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies.
